question_text: If (a + ib)² = x + iy, find x² + y².

mark_split.label: Take the modulus of both sides

recall_prompt: Say how you would find x² + y² without expanding the square — what you take on both sides and what that gives.
insider_note: This is a modulus question, not an expansion question: x² + y² is |x + iy|², so take the modulus of both sides and square to get (a² + b²)². Expanding, comparing parts, then squaring and adding reaches the same answer with four times the work.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Take the modulus
steps.margin_note: First mark. Do not expand. x² + y² is |x + iy|², so take the modulus of both sides: |(a + ib)²| = |a + ib|² = a² + b².

recall.must_convey: That taking the modulus of both sides gives |a + ib|² = |x + iy|, that is a² + b² = √(x² + y²).
accept: take modulus on both sides, mod of a plus i b squared is a squared plus b squared and mod of x plus i y is root x squared plus y squared
the modulus of the square is the square of the modulus, so a squared plus b squared equals root of x squared plus y squared
use mod of z squared equals mod z squared
rendu sides modulus teeste a square plus b square equals root x square plus y square
modulus both sides, a squared plus b squared on the left, root x squared plus y squared on the right
heard_as: root x squared plus y squared

steps.why: |z₁z₂| = |z₁||z₂|, so |z²| = |z|². The modulus turns the complex equation into a real one in a single line, which is why the question is worth 2 marks and not 4.
common_mistakes: Expanding (a + ib)², comparing parts, and then squaring and adding — correct but four times the work.

steps.label: Square both sides
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Square to remove the root on the right.

recall.must_convey: That squaring gives x² + y² = (a² + b²)².
accept: square both sides, x squared plus y squared equals a squared plus b squared whole square
x squared plus y squared is the square of a squared plus b squared
squaring removes the root, so a squared plus b squared whole squared
square cheste x square plus y square equals a square plus b square whole square
the answer is a squared plus b squared all squared
heard_as: a squared plus b squared squared

steps.why: The question asks for x² + y², which is the square of the right-hand modulus. One squaring finishes it; the answer is (a² + b²)², not a² + b².
common_mistakes: Stopping at a² + b² = √(x² + y²) and reporting a² + b² as the answer.
